change.author: Joe Au-Yeung

findings.title: Credential key is overwritten with a zod SafeParse result
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed value (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29). Line 97 assigns that to `key`, and line 98-101 writes it to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. Every Google token refresh therefore stores `{success:true,data:{...}}` in the credential. The next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` at line 75 throws, so the Google Calendar integration breaks for that user. This happens in the default setup, not only with credential sync. Use `.data` (it is already validated). Also, the parser mutates `data.refresh_token`, so check what ends up stored.

findings.title: Sync mode returns a fetch Response, but the code reads `res.data.access_token`
findings.body: With credential sync on, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` Response (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15). Line 94-96 reads `res?.data`, which is `undefined` on a Response, so `token.access_token` throws a TypeError. The catch at line 103 swallows it because the message is not `invalid_grant` and returns the unrefreshed client. The refresh never works and nothing is logged. The Response needs `.json()` and validation before the fields are used.

findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys that evaluate to "[object Object]"
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` is the literal property name `"[object Object]"`, because `ZodString#toString` is the default object `toString`. The same applies to line 10. The schema therefore requires a numeric property literally named `"[object Object]"`. The sync-endpoint path (line 15-16) can never succeed, and every refresh with credential sync enabled throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". The intended "any numeric field is the expiry" and "allow extra fields" semantics need `.passthrough()` with a `.refine`, or an explicit `expiry_date`/`expires_in` field. Strip mode also drops unknown fields, so extras are not kept.

findings.title: Helper now throws on invalid tokens, so callers' `!success` branches are dead and behaviour changed
findings.body: Line 21-23 throws when parsing fails, but callers still check `.success` afterwards: zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:108, salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:92, office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264. Those branches are unreachable. In Office 365 the old code logged the zod error and the MS response and continued. It now throws without logging either, so the MS payload and zod error are lost, and `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` is always true. Decide on one contract: throw and drop the dead checks, or return the result and let callers handle it.

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token "refresh_token" is injected into data in non-sync mode too
findings.body: Lines 25-27 set `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` whenever it is missing. That is not limited to the sync path. With the default schema and a provider that does not return a new refresh token on refresh (Google, Microsoft and Salesforce commonly omit it), a placeholder can be persisted and later sent as the refresh token. Salesforce overrides it explicitly (salesforce CalendarService.ts:98) but the other callers do not. Apply the placeholder only on the sync path, and keep the existing refresh token otherwise.

findings.title: `prisma` is used but never imported
findings.body: Line 96 calls `prisma.credential.update`, but the file has no `prisma` import (the only match is the call itself). This fails type-checking, and at runtime it throws `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` on every Salesforce service construction. `getClient` then rejects, and so do all later `await this.conn` calls.

findings.title: Salesforce now refreshes the token unconditionally on every construction, bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, and then ignores the new token
findings.body: The PR adds an unconditional refresh POST to login.salesforce.com inside `getClient`, which the constructor calls (line 57). This runs on every instantiation, not only when the token is expired. It does not go through `refreshOAuthTokens` (so credential sync is not honoured for Salesforce), and it is a new network call and DB write on each booking and availability lookup. It then builds the jsforce Connection with the stale `credentialKey.access_token` (line 106) instead of the freshly fetched `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`. The saved credential and the connection disagree. The refresh also overwrites the stored key with `salesforceTokenSchema` output, which drops any fields not in the schema. This looks like unrelated/accidental logic; if intended, route it through `refreshOAuthTokens` and use the new access token.

findings.title: Sync mode returns a Response that is used as a HubspotToken
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw fetch Response when sync is enabled. Line 177 types it as `HubspotToken`. Line 192 then computes `expiresIn * 1000` (NaN), and line 198 writes the Response object into `credential.key`. No parsing or validation is done. The same applies to zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:204-217 and zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:85-96, which read `.data.error` and `.data.expires_in` from the axios result. A fetch Response has no `.data`, so `tokenInfo.data.error` throws a TypeError. Each caller needs to convert the sync response (`await res.json()`) into the shape its normal path produces, or `refreshOAuthTokens` should return a normalised shape.

findings.title: Credential id passed as userId
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., credentialId)` has `userId` as its third parameter (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3). Line 93 passes `credentialId` (credential.id, line 53). In sync mode the endpoint receives `calcomUserId` set to the credential id, which is a different user or none. Pass `credential.userId`.

findings.title: appSlug "zoomvideo" does not match the Zoom app slug "zoom"
findings.body: The Zoom app metadata slug is `"zoom"` (packages/app-store/zoomvideo/_metadata.ts:16). The directory name is `zoomvideo`. The webhook resolves apps via `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` and `prisma.app` slug (app-credential.ts:40-50). The sync endpoint is sent a slug that the webhook would reject with 404, and the sender would be unable to use the same slug for its callback. The other slugs match (`google-calendar`, `lark-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `webex`, `zohocrm`, `zoho-bigin`, `hubspot`). Use `"zoom"`.

findings.title: Unvalidated request handling returns 500 on malformed input, no method check
findings.body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` (line 31) throws a ZodError for a bad body, giving an unhandled 500 rather than 400. Use `safeParse`. `symmetricDecrypt` (line 57-59) and `JSON.parse` can throw on a bad ciphertext or wrong key length, also as 500 with no useful message. The handler accepts any HTTP method. Restrict it to POST. Wrap the decrypt/parse in try/catch and return 400.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with `!==` (not constant-time)
findings.body: The shared secret that gates writing arbitrary credentials for any user id is compared with `!==` (line 24-27). Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. The header may also be an array or undefined; normalise it before comparing. The endpoint can overwrite any user's credential key for any app, so the secret check is the only trust boundary.

findings.title: Updating credentials does not clear `invalid` and does not validate key shape
findings.body: Update (line 73-80) only sets `key`. A credential previously marked `invalid: true` (e.g. Google `invalid_grant`, googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:112-116) stays invalid after a fresh token is pushed. Also, the decrypted `keys` are stored without validating against the app's expected key schema. Consider setting `invalid: false` on update.

findings.title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is typed string | undefined, not boolean
findings.body: The `&&` of two env strings gives `string | undefined` (the encryption key value or `""`). A name that reads like a boolean holds a secret value, which is risky if it is ever logged or serialised from this shared constants module. Wrap it in `Boolean(...)`. Also the sync endpoint and the webhook both depend on separate env sets (`CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is checked only at the call sites).

findings.title: Unrelated hardcoding of slug in redirect URI
findings.body: The redirect URI now hardcodes `zoho-bigin` instead of `appConfig.slug`, though `appConfig` is still imported and used at lines 12 and 22. This is an unrelated change that adds a second place to keep in sync with the slug.

findings.title: Redundant relative path inside the same folder
findings.body: `../oauth/decodeOAuthState` from within `_utils/oauth/` resolves to the sibling `./decodeOAuthState`. Use the direct `./decodeOAuthState` import.

findings.title: No tests for the new webhook or the refresh helpers
findings.body: The PR adds an auth-sensitive credential-writing endpoint and a token-refresh wrapper used by 10 integrations. It has no tests. A basic unit test of `parseRefreshTokenResponse` would have caught the `[object Object]` schema key and the SafeParse-as-key bug.

contracts.action: Credential sync webhook writes decrypted credential keys for a user/app
contracts.equivalent_path: Existing OAuth callbacks create credentials via createOAuthAppCredential (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts)
contracts.before_after: Callbacks check session and team admin access. The webhook relies only on a shared header secret, then looks up the user/app, decrypts the key and creates or updates the credential row.
contracts.visible_effect: The integration appears installed for the user, or its tokens are replaced, with no UI action
contracts.failure_mode: Bad body, decrypt failure or JSON parse failure throws, giving an unhandled 500. A stale `invalid` flag is not reset. The secret is compared non-constant-time.

contracts.action: Token refresh routed through refreshOAuthTokens and parseRefreshTokenResponse
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous direct refresh calls in each CalendarService/VideoApiAdapter
contracts.before_after: Before: provider refresh then schema parse. After: provider refresh or sync endpoint fetch, then a helper that returns a SafeParse result and throws on failure. Several callers treat the result as a parsed value or an axios/googleapis response.
contracts.visible_effect: Calendar/video/CRM integrations either stop refreshing silently (Google, Hubspot, Zoho) or store a corrupted key (Google)
contracts.failure_mode: In Google the SafeParse object is written to credential.key, so the next parse fails. In sync mode the Response lacks `.data`, so callers throw or save garbage. The Google catch swallows errors.

contracts.action: Salesforce getClient now performs a token refresh and DB update on every construction
contracts.equivalent_path: Other services refresh only when the token is expired (e.g. zoomvideo getToken, office365 getToken)
contracts.before_after: Before: jsforce Connection built with stored tokens. After: always POST to Salesforce and update the DB, then build the connection with the old access token. `prisma` is not imported.
contracts.visible_effect: Salesforce service construction throws ReferenceError, so bookings with Salesforce fail to sync
contracts.failure_mode: The constructor's promise rejects (line 57). Errors surface on later `await this.conn`.

summary: The PR cannot merge as is. The shared helper `parseRefreshTokenResponse` has a schema whose keys evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", so credential sync never works. Google Calendar stores a zod SafeParse object as the credential key, which breaks every Google refresh in the default setup. The Salesforce service uses `prisma` without importing it, and it now refreshes tokens on every construction. The sync path returns a fetch Response where Hubspot, Zoho and Google read `.data`. Smaller problems: Zoho Bigin passes the credential id as the user id, the Zoom slug is wrong ("zoomvideo" instead of "zoom"), and the webhook has weak input validation and a non-constant-time secret check. There are no tests.
